title: Bonded Titles for Boats and Watercraft
excerpt: Most states title boats over a certain length or engine size, which means a missing boat title can be bonded like a car's. A few states do not title boats at all.
metaDescription: How a bonded title works for a boat: which vessels states title, how the bond amount is set, and why registration and title are not the same thing.

body.text: Most states title boats above a certain length or engine size, and where a boat is titled, a missing title can be replaced with a surety bond the same way a car's can. Where a boat is only registered rather than titled, there is no title to bond and the route is different.

This trips up more boat owners than anything else. Registration is permission to operate on the water and is renewed periodically. Title is the record of who owns the vessel. A boat can be registered in your name and still have no title record, or a title record in somebody else's name.

So the first question is whether your state titles your vessel at all. Thresholds vary by length, by propulsion and by year, and some states title no boats whatsoever. Your state's agency is the authority; the [state motor vehicle directory](https://www.usa.gov/state-motor-vehicle-services) is the shortest route to it.

A boat and its trailer are usually titled separately, and losing one set of paperwork does not mean losing the other. If both are missing you may need two bonds, because they are two pieces of titled property with two values.

This surprises people who think of the rig as one item. It is worth confirming before you apply, because the trailer's bond is typically small and inexpensive. [Registering a vehicle, trailer or boat without a title](/how-am-i-going-to-register-my-vehicle-trailer-or-boat-in-alabama-without-a-proper-title) works through one state's version.

As with a vehicle, the bond is a multiple of the vessel's value. Valuing a boat is less standardised than valuing a car: price guides exist for common production hulls, but older, custom and homebuilt vessels usually need a marine survey or a dealer appraisal.

The hull identification number does for a boat what a VIN does for a car, and your state will want it on the application. [How your bond amount is determined](/how-your-bond-amount-is-determined) covers the valuation methods in more detail.

A vessel documented with the US Coast Guard is a separate system from state titling, and a missing document is a federal matter rather than a state one. If your boat is federally documented, a state title bond is not the remedy.
For everything else, the process is the ordinary one: see [how to get a bonded title](/how-to-get-a-bonded-title), and check your state's page for its multiplier and term.
